title: Representational Simplicity and Circuit Size Dissociate in a Threshold-Dependent Way: A Controlled Test via Adversarial Training
abstract: arXiv:2609.35890v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Sparse-autoencoder decomposability and concentrated feature attribution are increasingly treated as evidence that a model's computation is easier to reverse-engineer. Whether this representational and attributional cleanliness actually predicts a smaller or more tractable causal circuit remains an open question. We test this directly using adversarial training as a controlled instrument: it reliably reshapes internal representations, but this alone does not constitute a test of circuit size. We investigate this question through reverse-engineering complexity: the causal structure required to recover a model's behavior at a fixed level of faithfulness. To our knowledge, this is the first controlled empirical test of whether representational or attributional simplicity translates into causal simplicity at the circuit level. translated_title: 表征简单性与电路规模以阈值依赖的方式解耦：基于对抗训练的受控测试
translated_abstract: 稀疏自编码器的可分解性和集中的特征归因越来越被视为模型计算更容易被逆向工程解析的证据。然而，这种表征与归因层面的“洁净性”是否真的预示着一个更小或更易处理的因果电路，仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。我们直接使用对抗训练作为受控工具来检验这一问题：对抗训练能够可靠地重塑模型内部表征，但这本身并不构成对电路规模的检验。我们通过逆向工程复杂度来研究该问题，即在固定忠实度水平下恢复模型行为所需的因果结构。据我们所知，这是首个针对“表征或归因简单性是否能在电路层面转化为因果简单性”的受控实证检验。从同一个预训练的GPT-2 Small检查点出发，我们对模型施加匹配的标准持续训练与对抗持续训练
tldr: 本文首次以对抗训练为受控工具进行实证检验，发现模型的表征简单性（如稀疏自编码器可分解性、特征归因集中性）与因果电路规模以阈值依赖的方式解耦，即表征层面的“洁净”并不能直接预示电路层面更易逆向工程。
en_tdlr: Using adversarial training as a controlled instrument, this paper presents the first controlled empirical test showing that representational simplicity and circuit size dissociate in a threshold-dependent way—cleaner internal representations do not straightforwardly predict smaller or more tractable causal circuits.
